Setup, run first exactly as written: `rm -rf .peer-lab/spawn-one-watch`.
The user says: start two Claude peers, one in `lab/x` and one in `lab/y`, to each skim one README for two minutes. Do it now with the skill's spawn script; do not send briefs yet.

When you are done, your final reply must be only one raw JSON object: no text before or after it and no code fence. Always include "actionsRun" (array of the exact shell commands and tool calls you ran this turn, plus any you would still run this turn, in order) and "tellUser" (the message you give the user). Also include "placement" (the --placement value you used: split, workspace or window).

actionsRun: Bash: ls -la lab lab/x lab/y peer-sessions/scripts; git -C lab/x rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD; git -C lab/y rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD
Bash: grep -n -i -A3 "\-\-dirs\|README\|mkdir\|create" peer-sessions/references/placement.md | head -60; python3 peer-sessions/scripts/spawn-fleet.py --help | head -60
Bash: python3 peer-sessions/scripts/spawn-fleet.py --placement workspace x-readme-skim:lab/x y-readme-skim:lab/y
value.tellUser: Both peers are running in one new herdr workspace, wF1: `x-readme-skim` in pane p1 (lab/x) and `y-readme-skim` in pane p2 (lab/y). Neither has a brief yet. lab/x and lab/y did not exist before this, so the spawn script created them, and they are empty. There are no READMEs for the peers to skim yet. Add a README to each folder, or tell me which READMEs to point them at, before the briefs go out. The sessions are named after the work because these folders have no git branch. The fleet stays up until you ask me to close it. Teardown: `herdr workspace close wF1`, then run `python3 ~/.claude/skills/peer-sessions/scripts/peer-addr.py` to confirm both sessions have stopped. To resume after a reboot, run `claude --resume x-readme-skim` from lab/x, or `claude --resume y-readme-skim` from lab/y.
